rationale: The recordings have no artifact rejection, so a few eye blinks, movement or electrode-pop segments can inflate the Welch mean, especially in delta/theta and gamma. I'm switching Welch to median averaging across the 2-s segments (`average="median"`), which ignores those outlier windows. This should give cleaner relative band power estimates that also hold up better on other clinics' recordings. I haven't run it, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm re-referencing every recording to the common average (subtracting the per-sample mean across the 19 channels) before the median-Welch PSD. Relative power at each electrode depends on the original reference: activity at the reference site leaks into every channel, and the external Mumtaz data uses a different amplifier and reference. A common average reference should make the spectral topography more consistent across clinics, and it may sharpen the localized alpha and theta differences linked to MDD. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm adding a per-channel aperiodic (1/f) exponent for each condition alongside the relative band powers. It's the slope of a log-log fit to the median-Welch PSD over 2–40 Hz, leaving out the 7–14 Hz alpha peak. In MDD the spectrum is often flatter or steeper, which is read as an excitation/inhibition imbalance. Fixed bands mix this background slope with the oscillatory peaks, so a separate slope feature should add signal. It also doesn't depend on amplitude scale, so it should carry over to other amplifiers. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm adding a functional-connectivity feature: per-channel coherence strength (mean magnitude-squared coherence with the other 18 channels, Fisher-transformed) in the theta, alpha and beta bands for each condition. The literature links MDD to higher frontal and interhemispheric alpha/theta coherence, and the current power and slope features describe each channel on its own, so they can't capture synchrony between channels. Coherence is also unaffected by amplitude scale. Before computing coherence I drop 2-s segments whose broadband power is a robust outlier, which keeps the median-Welch artifact robustness. Using node strength instead of all 171 channel pairs keeps the number of added features small for a small sample. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm adding a per-channel weighted phase-lag index (wPLI) strength in the theta, alpha and beta bands, per condition. It reuses the cross-spectra from the artifact-screened 2-s segments that the coherence features already use. Coherence (kept in round 4, +0.054) mixes true coupling with zero-lag effects from volume conduction and the shared reference, and round 2 showed how strongly the reference affects these features. wPLI keeps only non-zero-lag phase coupling, so it should add separate MDD connectivity signal that also holds up under reference and amplifier changes. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

The feature set grew from about 100 to about 340 standardized features (relative power, 1/f slope and coherence strength in both conditions), but the L2 strength is still the C=0.1 picked for the first small feature set. I'm now choosing C on each training fold with an inner grouped 5-fold CV over a log grid, scored by AUROC. This should match the regularization to the larger, more correlated feature set without using the Dev score. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm adding a per-channel individual alpha peak frequency for each condition. It is the centre of gravity over 7–14 Hz of the PSD power that sits above the fitted 1/f (aperiodic) background. MDD is linked to a slower alpha peak, and a linear model on band powers cannot express a peak shift, so this should add new signal. The feature does not depend on amplitude scale or recording length, so it should carry over to the external clinic. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm adding a per-channel Higuchi fractal dimension for each condition. It is computed on a 1–45 Hz band-passed signal and taken as the median over 4-s epochs. Higher HFD in resting EEG is one of the most consistently reported MDD markers (Bachmann, Hosseinifard, Mumtaz). It measures nonlinear waveform complexity, which band power, the 1/f slope and coherence don't capture. It doesn't depend on amplitude scale, and the median over epochs keeps it robust to artifacts and recording length. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Coherence strength gave the largest gain so far (+0.054). But node strength averages each channel's coupling with all 18 others, which blurs the most consistently reported MDD connectivity finding: higher interhemispheric coherence between homologous left/right electrodes (Fp1-Fp2, F3-F4, F7-F8, C3-C4, T7-T8, P3-P4, P7-P8, O1-O2) in theta and alpha. This change reuses the same artifact-screened cross-spectra to add Fisher-transformed coherence for these up to 8 pairs, in the theta, alpha and beta bands, for each condition. That is at most 48 targeted features, and like the existing coherence features they do not depend on amplitude scale. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Coherence strength gave the biggest gain (+0.054), but it reduces each channel to one number. Fixed single-pair additions (round 9) and inner-CV tuning of C (round 6) both lowered the score. This round adds a second L2 logistic regression on the full band-limited correlation matrices (from the same artifact-screened cross-spectra, in theta, alpha and beta, for each condition). The matrices are mapped into Riemannian tangent space using a reference matrix fitted on the training fold only. Its probability is averaged with the current model's, so the whole network pattern can contribute without its roughly 1100 features drowning out the existing 380. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

I'm splitting the 8–13 Hz alpha band used for connectivity (coherence strength and the Riemannian correlation matrices) into low alpha (8–10 Hz) and high alpha (10–13 Hz). Low alpha is widespread and tracks arousal/vigilance, which is thought to be altered in MDD, while high alpha is more local and task-related. A single wide band averages these two kinds of coupling together. The change reuses the same artifact-screened cross-spectra and stays independent of amplitude scale. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Splitting alpha into low and high alpha for connectivity helped in round 11, so this round splits the 13–30 Hz connectivity band into low beta (13–20 Hz) and high beta (20–30 Hz), for both coherence strength and the Riemannian correlation matrices. Low-beta coupling is cortical (sensorimotor/frontal rhythms, raised in MDD), while high-beta coupling is mixed with scalp-muscle (EMG) activity that is broadband and correlated across channels. One wide band blends the real coupling with that artifact, and separate bands let each model weight them on their own. This hasn't been run yet, so there's no Dev score for it.

This round adds EEG microstate features to the base logistic regression: coverage, log mean duration and occurrence for each class, plus the 12 between-class transition probabilities, for each condition. They come from 4 polarity-invariant template maps fitted label-free on 2–20 Hz GFP-peak topographies, with artifact peaks removed. MDD is reported to change microstate dynamics, especially the balance between classes C and D, and these are temporal features that the current spectral and connectivity features cannot represent. They also don't depend on amplitude scale or the original reference, so they should carry over to the external clinic. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Round 11 showed that splitting alpha into low (8–10 Hz) and high (10–13 Hz) helps for connectivity, but the relative band-power features still use one 8–13 Hz band. This round applies the same split to the per-channel log relative power, testing whether MDD changes the balance between widespread low alpha, which tracks arousal/vigilance, and more local high alpha in a way one wide alpha band averages out. The change adds only 19 scale-invariant features per condition, and they come from the existing median-Welch PSD.

I'm adding one feature per channel and condition: log total 1–45 Hz power minus that subject's mean across channels. This tests whether depression is reflected in how absolute power is distributed across the scalp, for example frontal versus posterior; the theta "cordance" depression marker combines this with relative power. Relative power is normalized within each channel, so it removes that across-scalp information, and subtracting the subject's channel mean keeps the new features independent of amplifier gain (38 features).

This round adds per-channel amplitude-envelope correlation strength, in theta, low alpha, high alpha and beta, to the base model. It is a mean Fisher-z correlation of log Hilbert-envelope time courses over 0.5-s windows, with artifact windows dropped. Depression is linked to altered slow co-fluctuation of oscillation amplitude across regions, which spectral coherence (phase-locked spectra over 2-s windows) does not capture. Correlating log envelopes also leaves out amplifier gain.

Last round's per-channel envelope-correlation strength gave the biggest gain since round 4 (+0.011), but it reduces each channel to one number. Round 10 found that the full coherence correlation matrices, projected into Riemannian tangent space, added signal beyond node strength. This change does the same for the envelope network: the shrunk log-envelope correlation matrices (theta, low alpha, high alpha, beta, per condition) go into the existing Riemannian branch as extra blocks. That lets the model use the specific region-to-region amplitude co-fluctuation pattern while keeping the 50/50 fusion weights the same. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Linkenkaer-Hansen et al. (2005) reported that long-range temporal correlations in oscillation amplitude break down in MDD. Nothing in the current model measures this: it describes how band power and coupling are distributed, not how amplitude evolves over seconds. This round adds a per-channel detrended-fluctuation-analysis (DFA) exponent of the theta, low-alpha, high-alpha and beta amplitude envelopes for each condition. The envelopes are reused from `_envelope`, downsampled to 10 Hz, and fitted over 1–12 s scales. Window fluctuations are aggregated by their median so artifacts have less effect. The exponent does not depend on amplifier gain. The change adds 152 features to the base logistic regression. I haven't run it, so there is no Dev score yet.

This round adds per-channel orthogonalized amplitude-envelope correlation strength (Hipp et al. 2012) to the base logistic regression, in theta, low alpha, high alpha and beta for each condition. Plain envelope correlation gave the largest recent gains (rounds 16–17), but part of it may come from zero-lag field spread and the shared reference. Orthogonalizing each channel's analytic signal against a seed channel before correlating the envelopes removes that instantaneous leakage. That isolates true long-range amplitude coupling, which should also hold up better under a different reference or amplifier at the external clinic. I haven't run this version, so I don't have a Dev score for it yet.

Last round's orthogonalized envelope-correlation strength (+0.0056) still reduces each channel to a single number. When the plain envelope network went from node strength into the Riemannian tangent-space branch (rounds 16→17), it added +0.0066. This round does the same for the orthogonalized envelope-correlation matrices (theta, low alpha, high alpha, beta, per condition). They are symmetrized, eigenvalue-clipped to be valid correlation matrices, and shrunk, so the model can use the region-to-region amplitude coupling pattern with zero-lag leakage removed. I haven't run this version, so there is no Dev score yet.
